extraction.name: BoolQ
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset of naturally occurring yes/no questions generated in unprompted and unconstrained settings, paired with paragraphs from Wikipedia.
extraction.creator: Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, Ming-Wei Chang, Tom Kwiatkowski, Michael Collins, Kristina Toutanova
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are gathered from anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine. Queries likely to be yes/no questions are heuristically identified and kept if a Wikipedia page is returned as one of the first five results. The question and Wikipedia page are then given to a human annotator for further processing.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine and Wikipedia articles.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries are heuristically filtered by checking if the first word is in a manually constructed set of indicator words and if they are of sufficient length. Questions are only kept if a Wikipedia page is returned in the top five results. Only questions marked as having a yes/no answer are used, and each is paired with the selected passage instead of the entire document.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators label question/article pairs in a three-step process: 1) decide if the question is good (comprehensible, unambiguous, requesting factual information), 2) find a passage within the document containing enough information to answer the question (or mark as 'not answerable'), 3) mark whether the question's answer is 'yes' or 'no'.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Three authors labelled 110 randomly chosen examples to assess quality, reaching 90% accuracy compared to gold-standard labels. Disagreements were resolved by mutual agreement; six were ambiguous/debatable cases, and five were annotator errors.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: 'Yes' answers are slightly more common (62.31% in the train set). There is a weak correlation between the nature of the question and the likelihood of a 'yes' answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions are limited to those where a Wikipedia page is returned in the top five search results. Question-only models perform very poorly, meaning questions do not contain sufficient information to predict the answer on their own.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. Used to test models on their ability to answer naturally occurring yes/no questions and make complex inferences.
